subject: biology-9
description: Sources of genetic variation, gene mutations, Darwin's theory of natural selection, homologous and analogous structures, speciation, and evolutionary evidence.

questions.question: In a population, genetic variation is critical because it

options.A: Causes individuals to grow faster regardless of conditions
options.B: Provides different traits that can be favored by natural selection
options.C: Always leads to harmful mutations

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option B ('Provides different traits that can be favored by natural selection') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Evolution can best be described as

options.A: A temporary shift in the structure of DNA during an organism's life
options.B: The gradual development of new species over generations through inherited changes
options.C: The sudden appearance of entirely new species without common ancestors

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option B ('The gradual development of new species over generations through inherited changes') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Discontinuous variation is observed in traits such as

options.A: Height and skin color, which vary continuously
options.B: Blood groups and tongue-rolling ability, with distinct categories
options.C: Traits that result only from environmental changes

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option B ('Blood groups and tongue-rolling ability, with distinct categories') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Mutation contributes to evolution because

options.A: It always leads to the extinction of a species
options.B: It introduces new alleles into a population's gene pool
options.C: It prevents any further variation from occurring

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option B ('It introduces new alleles into a population's gene pool') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Variations that occur due to genetic changes

options.A: Can be inherited and may influence evolution
options.B: Are always harmful and short-lived
options.C: Never affect reproductive success

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Can be inherited and may influence evolution') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Continuous variation is typically seen in traits such as

options.A: Eye color, which has clear categories
options.B: Fingerprint patterns that are uniform across populations
options.C: Height and weight, which show a range of values

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option C ('Height and weight, which show a range of values') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Natural selection operates by

options.A: Randomly eliminating all traits in a population
options.B: Favoring individuals with characteristics that improve survival and reproduction
options.C: Ensuring that all organisms evolve at the same rate

questions.explanation: THEORY OF NATURAL SELECTION

questions.question: Darwin’s theory of natural selection emphasizes that

options.A: Offspring inherit all acquired characteristics
options.B: Only the strongest individuals survive regardless of adaptation
options.C: Organisms with beneficial traits are more likely to survive and reproduce

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option C ('Organisms with beneficial traits are more likely to survive and reproduce') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: A major concept of natural selection is that

options.A: Overproduction leads to competition, which determines survival
options.B: All individuals in a population have an equal chance of survival
options.C: Traits acquired during an organism’s life are passed on

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Overproduction leads to competition, which determines survival') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Natural selection may lead to evolution when

options.A: Certain inherited traits become more common over generations
options.B: All individuals are cloned to maintain genetic uniformity
options.C: Environmental changes no longer influence survival

questions.explanation: EVIDENCES OF EVOLUTION

questions.question: The fossil record supports the theory of evolution by

options.A: Showing that all species appeared simultaneously
options.B: Providing a chronological sequence of organisms through geological layers
options.C: Proving that ancient organisms were always more complex

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option B ('Providing a chronological sequence of organisms through geological layers') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Homologous structures in different species indicate that

options.A: These species evolved similar traits independently
options.B: They may have evolved from a common ancestor
options.C: They are unrelated but live in similar environments

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option B ('They may have evolved from a common ancestor') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Comparative anatomy supports evolution because

options.A: Similar internal structures can be found in organisms with different functions
options.B: Different species always have identical external appearances
options.C: All organisms have unique body plans without any similarity

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Similar internal structures can be found in organisms with different functions') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Selective breeding in agriculture shows that

options.A: Evolution can be directed by human selection of traits over generations
options.B: Traits in plants and animals arise randomly without influence
options.C: All offspring will have the same traits as their parents

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Evolution can be directed by human selection of traits over generations') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Fossil evidence is particularly useful because it

options.A: Shows extinct organisms and transitional forms between species
options.B: Confirms that species never changed over time
options.C: Can only be used to study living species

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Shows extinct organisms and transitional forms between species') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Analogous structures, such as wings of insects and birds, provide evidence that

options.A: Similar environmental pressures can result in similar functions through different structures
options.B: All organisms have a shared evolutionary origin
options.C: Evolution only occurs in animals with wings

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Similar environmental pressures can result in similar functions through different structures') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Artificial selection differs from natural selection in that

options.A: It is random and does not rely on inherited traits
options.B: It involves human intervention to promote desirable traits
options.C: It prevents organisms from adapting to the environment

questions.explanation: NATURAL SELECTION VS ARTIFICIAL SELECTION

questions.question: In natural selection, the traits that increase survival are

options.A: Often passed on because individuals with them reproduce more
options.B: Always determined by human needs
options.C: Not influenced by the environment at all

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Often passed on because individuals with them reproduce more') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: A major difference between artificial and natural selection is that

options.A: Artificial selection occurs naturally over long periods
options.B: Natural selection is purposeful and directed by humans
options.C: Artificial selection is controlled by humans to obtain specific characteristics

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option C ('Artificial selection is controlled by humans to obtain specific characteristics') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Artificial selection has allowed humans to

options.A: Change species by choosing specific traits for reproduction
options.B: Eliminate genetic variation in populations completely
options.C: Make organisms immune to all environmental changes

questions.explanation: SPECIATION

questions.question: Speciation is a process that results in

options.A: The formation of new species through reproductive isolation and genetic divergence
options.B: The merging of all populations into one species
options.C: The elimination of mutations from a gene pool

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('The formation of new species through reproductive isolation and genetic divergence') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Geographic isolation may lead to speciation when

options.A: Populations adapt differently due to environmental differences and cannot interbreed
options.B: All individuals move to a single area
options.C: The gene pool of both populations becomes identical

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Populations adapt differently due to environmental differences and cannot interbreed') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Reproductive isolation occurs when

options.A: Members of different populations can no longer produce fertile offspring
options.B: All organisms breed with one another without restriction
options.C: Breeding occurs at the same time of year across all populations

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Members of different populations can no longer produce fertile offspring') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Behavioral isolation can result in speciation when

options.A: Differences in mating behavior prevent interbreeding between populations
options.B: Physical barriers disappear
options.C: All species share identical mating rituals

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Differences in mating behavior prevent interbreeding between populations') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Speciation is unlikely to happen if

options.A: Populations frequently interbreed and exchange genes
options.B: Different environmental pressures act on isolated populations
options.C: Genetic drift occurs in small populations

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Populations frequently interbreed and exchange genes') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Over time, genetic divergence between isolated populations

options.A: May lead to the evolution of new species if reproductive isolation is maintained
options.B: Causes all traits to become uniform
options.C: Prevents evolution from occurring

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('May lead to the evolution of new species if reproductive isolation is maintained') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Temporal isolation contributes to speciation by

options.A: Preventing reproduction due to different mating times among populations
options.B: Making all organisms breed at the same time
options.C: Eliminating behavioral differences between populations

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Preventing reproduction due to different mating times among populations') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: In sympatric speciation, new species arise

options.A: Within the same geographical area due to genetic changes and reproductive barriers
options.B: Only after a physical barrier separates populations
options.C: When individuals migrate to different continents

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Within the same geographical area due to genetic changes and reproductive barriers') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Speciation due to genetic drift is more common in

options.A: Small, isolated populations where chance events affect allele frequencies
options.B: Large populations with stable gene pools
options.C: Populations with identical genetic structures

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Small, isolated populations where chance events affect allele frequencies') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.

questions.question: Speciation is complete when

options.A: Populations are reproductively isolated and cannot produce fertile offspring
options.B: All individuals in both groups continue interbreeding
options.C: Both populations have identical physical traits

questions.explanation: According to FBISE Class 9 Biology curriculum standards, Option A ('Populations are reproductively isolated and cannot produce fertile offspring') is the correct biological fact for Variation, Natural Selection & Evolution.
